entries.title: Start with Simple Map

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose Simple Map
requiredGuideSteps.body: On first launch, select Simple Map. Later, you can change it in Settings without deleting maps or records.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Allow location access
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open the map and approve location access when asked. Go outdoors and wait briefly for the first accurate fix.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Learn the four controls
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Locate, Add Pin, Record and More. More contains measurement, basemap and offline map tools.

entries.title: Import a PDF or map file

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open Import
requiredGuideSteps.body: From the map or Library, open Import Map.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose the source
requiredGuideSteps.body: Pick a PDF/GeoPDF, GeoTIFF, image, KMZ, web link or QR code.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Check the map position
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open the imported map and tap Locate. If an older imported PDF is misaligned, delete that copy and import it again so the current georeference parser runs.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Use Open in MapNero
requiredGuideSteps.body: You can also select a supported file in the Files app and share or open it with MapNero.

entries.title: Reference a photo manually

requiredGuideSteps.title: Import the image
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose Import Photo as Map, then begin the manual reference option.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Place known control points
requiredGuideSteps.body: For each point, tap the same identifiable place on the image and on the base map. Spread points around the image rather than along one edge.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Check before relying on it
requiredGuideSteps.body: Review the fit and open the saved map. In Library, the MAN badge confirms that the map was referenced manually.

entries.title: Find your location and record a track

requiredGuideSteps.title: Centre the map
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Locate. Tap it again to change the follow state if you want the map to remain centred while moving.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Start recording
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Record, confirm the recording state, then begin moving.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Watch the live line
requiredGuideSteps.body: The recording line updates on the Base Map and imported PDF maps while recording.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Stop and save
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap the square Stop button to finish recording; the track is saved automatically. Review it later in the Library or its layer.

entries.title: Add pins and manage layers

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose a visible layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Layers and select a normal writable layer. Turn its visibility on.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Add the pin
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Add Pin or long-press the map, then choose the pin type.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Describe the record
requiredGuideSteps.body: Add a name, notes, attributes or media, then save.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Edit later
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap the feature on the map and open Edit from its detail card.

entries.title: Download a map for offline use

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open Offline Maps
requiredGuideSteps.body: On Base Map, move and zoom to the field area first. Then tap Offline Maps in the map controls; if needed, open More.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Frame the work area
requiredGuideSteps.body: The download uses the visible Base Map area when Offline Maps opens. If it is wrong, close the screen, adjust the map, then open it again.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose detail and download
requiredGuideSteps.body: Select the zoom range, check the estimated size and start the download while online.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Test before leaving
requiredGuideSteps.body: Turn on Airplane Mode, reopen the region and confirm the required zoom levels are visible.

entries.title: Use map collections and Atlas

requiredGuideSteps.title: Group adjoining maps
requiredGuideSteps.body: In the Library, move georeferenced sheets into the same collection and place preferred detailed maps above fallback maps.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Browse across sheet edges
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open a collection map and pan the centre crosshair into a neighbouring sheet. The active sheet changes while the camera scale is preserved.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose GPS auto-switch only if needed
requiredGuideSteps.body: Manual centre browsing is on by default. GPS-based Auto-switch is separate and off by default in Map Collections settings.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create an Atlas
requiredGuideSteps.body: With an offline raster MBTiles basemap active, open Create PDF Map, enable Atlas collection, choose scale and overlap, then create up to 64 sheets.

entries.title: Measure, draw a bearing and create a buffer

requiredGuideSteps.title: Measure on the map
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open More → Measure, place points and read the live line length or area.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create by bearing and distance
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open More → COGO, enter a base point or use the current GPS fix, then enter a 0–360° grid bearing and a distance up to 100 km.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create a buffer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open a point, line, track, polygon or circle, tap Buffer, enter metres, choose fill colour and opacity, then create.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Edit the result
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open the buffer in Derived Buffers to change distance, fill colour or opacity. Changing distance rebuilds it from the original feature.

entries.title: Create and edit a buffer

requiredGuideSteps.title: Select the source
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap a feature on the map, or open Layers and select a feature. In its detail card, choose Buffer; scroll the action row if necessary. This tool requires Pro or Team access.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set the distance
requiredGuideSteps.body: Enter a positive distance and choose metres or feet. You can give the output a name; leaving it empty keeps the automatic name.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Preview and style
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Preview to see how many sources and polygons can be processed. Preview does not save anything. Choose the fill colour and opacity before creating the buffer.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create the polygon
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose Create Buffer. The result goes into the separate Derived Buffers layer. Close the feature card to inspect it on the map; the original feature remains unchanged.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Edit or buffer several features
requiredGuideSteps.body: Select the saved buffer to change its colour, opacity or distance. Distance updates need the original source. For several features, use lasso selection and Buffer; check processed and skipped counts.

entries.title: Connect a team or external GNSS

requiredGuideSteps.title: Sign in
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Settings → Account, enter your email and complete the six-digit one-time code.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Join your organization
requiredGuideSteps.body: Accept an invitation or enter the organization code provided by its administrator.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Share a layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open a layer and enable Share with organization. Internet access is required for synchronization.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Pair external GNSS
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Settings → External GNSS, enable Bluetooth, choose your receiver and wait for a valid position and accuracy reading.

entries.title: Use EOD and mine-action records safely

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose the correct mode
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Settings and select the EOD or mine-action mode needed for the task.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Capture the field record
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Spot Report, Certificate or Land Release forms and complete the required source and location fields.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review before export
requiredGuideSteps.body: Check coordinates, units, attachments and organization fields before creating PDF or IMSMA XML output.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Use an approved authority
requiredGuideSteps.body: For safety distances or consequence analysis, follow your organization’s approved standard, qualified EOD/ESO review and authorized tools.

entries.title: Plan a route with waypoints

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open Route Builder
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose a visible, unlocked layer, then open More → Route Builder on the map.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Place the first point
requiredGuideSteps.body: Pan the map until the centre crosshair is over your starting point, then tap Add Waypoint. Your GPS position does not have to be there.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Extend and check the route
requiredGuideSteps.body: Move the crosshair and add at least one more point. Check the waypoint list and total distance. Use a row’s minus button to remove a mistaken point; the trash button clears the whole draft.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Save the route
requiredGuideSteps.body: With at least two points, use the green Save to Layer button. The builder closes and the route is stored in the target layer. Closing with X discards an unsaved draft.

entries.title: Inspect a track in 3D

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the track card
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Layers, open the layer containing your track and select the track. Tap 3D in its action row.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose a display
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Elevation, Speed or Route Only. Speed mode represents recorded speed, not terrain height; Route Only removes the vertical profile.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Inspect and return
requiredGuideSteps.body: The top-right rotation button stops or restarts automatic rotation. Drag to change the camera angle; use Back to return without editing the track.

entries.title: Read and share a track report

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open Analysis or Report
requiredGuideSteps.body: Select the track in its layer. Scroll the action row to More, then choose Analysis or Report. Report opens the detailed section; scroll up for the summary and graphs.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Compare the graphs
requiredGuideSteps.body: Review distance, duration, average speed and maximum elevation. Switch between Combined, Speed and Elevation; missing or constant input data limits what these graphs can tell you.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review the detailed figures
requiredGuideSteps.body: With Core or higher, inspect moving/paused time, pace, speed, elevation gain/loss and point count. These are calculated from the available track data, not independent measurements.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Prepare and share the PDF
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Share PDF in the report section. Wait for preparation, then choose a destination in the system share sheet. At least two track points are needed. Review locations and other details before sending.

entries.title: Follow a track with corridor alerts

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the saved line or track
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Layers, select a line or track with at least two points. In its detail card choose Track Navigation / Navigate Track.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set direction and alert corridor
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose Forward or Reverse, then set the alert distance from 5 m to 1000 m. The corridor is the distance from the line at which MapNero warns that you are off course.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Start, monitor and finish
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Start following. The map panel shows the next point, remaining on-route distance, deviation and progress. Use Pause when needed; use Stop to finish. Starting or stopping does not alter or record the source track.

entries.title: Create contours from an elevation GeoTIFF

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the GeoTIFF menu
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Library, find the imported GeoTIFF, open its More menu and choose Create contours.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose an interval
requiredGuideSteps.body: Select 5, 10, 20 or 50 metres. Use a wider interval for an overview and a tighter one only when the source resolution supports it.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create and check the layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose Create contours and keep MapNero open while processing finishes. A new editable contour layer is added to the same map; inspect it before field use and keep the original GeoTIFF.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Use or export carefully
requiredGuideSteps.body: You can style, edit, filter or export the resulting layer like other vector layers. Contours are derived data: verify their alignment, interval and source before sharing or using them for decisions.

entries.title: Inspect point clusters

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose the layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Layers, choose the relevant point layer. Analysis needs at least 8 points; lines and polygons are not its input.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the analysis
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open the layer’s (…) menu and choose Cluster Analysis. Pro or higher is required. Check the input point count before interpreting the distribution.

entries.title: Use Community Trails

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the catalogue
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Settings → Community Trails. You can search by route name, description or general region.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Download a route
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose Download to add an independent copy to Track Records. Later changes or removal of the public item do not alter your local copy.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Publish your track
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open a saved track, choose More → Community Trails, add a description, general region and licence, confirm the safety notice, then publish. Publishing requires a confirmed Core-or-higher account.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Control what you see
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use the item menu to report a route or block its author. You can remove routes you published. Shared data is limited to route points, name, description, general region and licence; photos and private feature fields are not included.

entries.title: Create attribute forms for a layer

requiredGuideSteps.title: Start from the layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Layers, choose a writable layer, then open its settings and Attribute Schema. Add the fields that belong to every feature, such as species, cover, status, notes or a date.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Or create a reusable template
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Templates and create a form with the fields your team needs. Use a template when the same form should be reused across more than one field workflow.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Bind the template to the layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Return to the layer’s settings, open Template Binding and choose the template. Its fields become the layer’s feature attribute schema.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Collect and review records
requiredGuideSteps.body: Add or edit a point, line or polygon in that layer and complete the form. Open the layer’s attribute table to search, filter and review saved records.

entries.title: Collect field data with a template

requiredGuideSteps.title: Find the template
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Templates, search or browse a category, then read the field list before starting. A template may include text, choices, numbers, GPS, date, photo and checklist fields.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Start the field workflow
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Play or Use Template. You can begin from the template library before opening a map. Complete required fields and allow GPS or camera access only when the form asks for them.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review the saved record
requiredGuideSteps.body: Submit the form, then open the created or selected layer to see the new feature and its attributes. Use the layer table to search or review results, and export only after checking the records.

entries.title: Create and edit a field template

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create the template
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Templates → Create. Choose Manual to build the form yourself; review every field before using an imported or store template.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Add the field structure
requiredGuideSteps.body: Give the template a clear name, then add text, choice, number, date, GPS, photo, checkbox or icon fields. For a choice field, enter the permitted values.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set the collection order
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open each field to set its label, help text, required state and options. Use the up/down controls to put fields in field-work order, save, then run one test entry.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Edit safely
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Library → Templates, open the template menu and choose Edit. Save the changes, reopen the template and use Play or Use Template for new records.

entries.title: Sync one layer with your account

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the layer editor
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Layers, select the layer, then choose Edit.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Enable Sync with my account
requiredGuideSteps.body: Below Lock layer, turn on Sync with my account and save the layer.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Continue on another device
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use the same signed-in MapNero account on Web GIS, iPhone, iPad or Android while online. The selected layer becomes available there after sync.

entries.title: Run a live Team Session

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create the session
requiredGuideSteps.body: Settings → Team Tracking. On a phone or tablet, open Team and choose Create session. A Team account can host. An organization is optional; attach one only when the session belongs to that organization.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set the access details
requiredGuideSteps.body: Give the session a clear field name and set the name that will appear on the map. Choose a session password; MapNero generates the session code after creation. Send the generated code and password only to invited participants.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Join and finish safely
requiredGuideSteps.body: Each participant chooses Join session or scans the QR code, then enters the code, password and display name. Core, Pro and Team accounts can join. When field work ends, the host ends the session and does not reuse its code.

entries.title: Export field data and share it safely

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose what to export
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open the layer, track, map or report and choose Export. Select only the records you intend to send; use a recorded track for GPX and a GIS format for vector features.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose a compatible format
requiredGuideSteps.body: KML, GPX, CSV and KMZ are available on Free. GeoPDF and GeoTIFF need Core or higher. Shapefile, GeoPackage, DXF and QGIS/QField bundle need Pro or higher.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review and deliver
requiredGuideSteps.body: Check the selected layers, attributes, coordinates and attachments before generating the file. Use the system share sheet for a local file, or Share via Link only after checking that temporary public download is suitable.

entries.title: Configure MapNero settings

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose a working mode
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Settings → Usage Mode. Simple Map keeps the main workspace uncluttered; a specialist mode or Custom exposes the tools you choose. Your saved maps, layers and records remain intact.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set language, appearance and units
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Settings, choose Language, Appearance, Display and Units of Measurement. Pick the coordinate format and units your team uses before recording values or sharing screenshots.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Tune map and symbol preferences
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Map Display for labels, grids, PDF boundary locking, collection behaviour and raster background choices. In Tools and Symbols, enable only the controls and symbol packs you want to see.

entries.title: Capture a watermarked field photo

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the field camera
requiredGuideSteps.body: From the map, open the Camera control. You can set reusable defaults in Settings → Photo Watermark.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose what the watermark shows
requiredGuideSteps.body: Turn fields such as timestamp, coordinate, heading, place name, project, note, compass, logo or mini-map on only when they are appropriate. Set the position and panel opacity.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Capture, review and save
requiredGuideSteps.body: Take a new photo or choose one from the gallery. Check the preview, edit fields or retake if needed, then save to Photos or share the finished image.

entries.title: Create a geofence

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open Geofences
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Settings → Geofences, or select a feature and choose Notify. Use a known location or wait for GPS before creating the boundary.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set the circle
requiredGuideSteps.body: Give it a clear name, choose the radius and colour, then select alerts for entry, exit or both. Confirm the centre before you create it.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Monitor and review
requiredGuideSteps.body: Keep the fence enabled and allow the requested location and notification permissions. Open Geofence History to review events; disable or remove a fence when it is no longer needed.

entries.title: GeoTIFF / PDF background

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the georeferenced map
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Map Library, open a GeoTIFF, GeoPDF or manually referenced map. An image without a geographic reference needs georeferencing first.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose the background
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open More (…). Under Map Background, choose Basemap to see the surrounding area or Blank Canvas to hide it.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Adjust visibility
requiredGuideSteps.body: With Basemap selected, move the background visibility/opacity slider. A lower value makes the background less prominent. This does not edit the original file or your feature styles.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Find the map again
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Fit Map / fit to screen to return to the map’s extent. Locate centres on your current GPS position, which may be far outside this map.

entries.title: Create a GeoPDF map layout

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set the map view
requiredGuideSteps.body: On the Base Map, pan and zoom to the exact area you want on the page. Visible features are included; review sensitive pins and tracks before export.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Configure the layout
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose PDF, PNG or JPEG, page size and orientation. Add a title, author or project if needed, then choose elements such as legend, scale bar, north arrow, overview inset and UTM grid.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Export or build an Atlas
requiredGuideSteps.body: Create the file and review it before sending. For a multi-page Atlas, enable Atlas collection, choose scale and page overlap, and use a downloaded raster MBTiles basemap. Atlas creation needs Pro.

requiredGuideSteps.body: Complete the Spot Report, Certificate or Land Release fields, including source and location context.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review the export
requiredGuideSteps.body: Check coordinates, units, attachments and organization fields before producing PDF or IMSMA output.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Follow approved authority
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use your organization’s approved standards, qualified EOD/ESO review and authorized tools for operational decisions.

entries.title: Plan a route with waypoints

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open Route Builder
requiredGuideSteps.body: Select a visible, unlocked, writable feature layer. Open Route from the map toolbar or More menu, depending on your toolbar layout.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Place the first point
requiredGuideSteps.body: Pan the map until the centre crosshair is over your starting point, then tap Add Waypoint. Your GPS position does not have to be there.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Extend and check the route
requiredGuideSteps.body: Move the crosshair and add at least one more point. Check the waypoint list and total distance. Use a row’s minus button to remove a mistaken point; the trash button clears the whole draft.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Save the route
requiredGuideSteps.body: With at least two points, tap the green Save button (it may still say Save in another app language). The route is saved to the target layer. X closes the builder and discards an unsaved draft.

entries.title: Follow a track with corridor alerts

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the saved line or track
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Layers, select a line or track with at least two points. In its detail card choose Track Navigation / Navigate Track.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set direction and alert corridor
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose Forward or Reverse, then set the alert distance from 5 m to 1000 m. The corridor is the distance from the line at which MapNero warns that you are off course.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Start, monitor and finish
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Start following. The map panel shows the next point, remaining on-route distance, deviation and progress. Use Pause when needed; use Stop to finish. Starting or stopping does not alter or record the source track.

entries.title: Read and share a track report

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the recorded track
requiredGuideSteps.body: Select the track in its layer or on the map to open its feature details. With at least two points, scroll to Track Analysis and tap Track Report. The detailed report requires Core or higher.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review the report
requiredGuideSteps.body: Check the top-down route sketch, distance, point count, start/end coordinates, speed and elevation sections. The sketch here is 2D, not Apple’s interactive 3D viewer. Missing or constant altitude/speed values limit the analysis.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Interpret time carefully
requiredGuideSteps.body: In this version, moving time is the interval from the first GPS point to the last; paused time is the remaining part of the total recording duration. Stops within that point interval are not all removed. Do not interpret these as independently detected moving and stopped periods.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Share the PDF
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Share PDF at the bottom or the share icon at the top. After preparation, choose a destination in the system share sheet. Review coordinates and other details before sending. The file is a report, not a GPX track; first-time PDF preparation may need internet to load fonts.

entries.title: Preview a route in 3D

requiredGuideSteps.title: Prepare the route
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Route from the map toolbar or More and add at least two waypoints using the crosshair.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the preview
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap 3D inside the route panel. After elevation lookup, the screen shows a relief-style route image and elevation profile. This is not an interactive 3D drawing editor.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Return to the route
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Back to return to the draft; save it separately with Save. The map toolbar’s separate 3D button requires Core or higher and toggles map tilt; tap it again for a top-down view. You can also turn 3D Terrain on or off and set camera pitch in Settings > 3D & Terrain.

entries.title: Configure 3D Terrain

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open 3D Terrain
requiredGuideSteps.body: From the Library, open Settings > 3D & Terrain > 3D Terrain.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set camera pitch

entries.title: Inspect point clusters

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose the layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Layers, choose the relevant point layer. Analysis needs at least 8 points; lines and polygons are not its input.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the analysis

entries.title: Use Community Trails

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the catalogue
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Settings → Community Trails. You can search by route name, description or general region.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Download a route
requiredGuideSteps.body: Choose Download to add an independent copy to Track Records. Later changes or removal of the public item do not alter your local copy.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Publish your track
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open a saved track, choose More → Community Trails, add a description, general region and licence, confirm the safety notice, then publish. Publishing requires a confirmed Core-or-higher account.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Control what you see
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use the item menu to report a route or block its author. You can remove routes you published. Shared data is limited to route points, name, description, general region and licence; photos and private feature fields are not included.

entries.title: Create attribute forms for a layer

requiredGuideSteps.title: Start from the layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Layers, choose a writable layer, then open its settings and Attribute Schema. Add the fields that belong to every feature, such as species, cover, status, notes or a date.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Or create a reusable template
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Templates and create a form with the fields your team needs. Use a template when the same form should be reused across more than one field workflow.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Bind the template to the layer
requiredGuideSteps.body: Return to the layer’s settings, open Template Binding and choose the template. Its fields become the layer’s feature attribute schema.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Collect and review records
requiredGuideSteps.body: Add or edit a point, line or polygon in that layer and complete the form. Open the layer’s attribute table to search, filter and review saved records.

entries.title: Collect field data with a template

requiredGuideSteps.title: Find the template
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Templates, search or browse a category, then read the field list before starting. A template may include text, choices, numbers, GPS, date, photo and checklist fields.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Start the field workflow
requiredGuideSteps.body: Tap Play or Use Template. You can begin from the template library before opening a map. Complete required fields and allow GPS or camera access only when the form asks for them.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review the saved record
requiredGuideSteps.body: Submit the form, then open the created or selected layer to see the new feature and its attributes. Use the layer table to search or review results, and export only after checking the records.

entries.title: Create and edit a field template

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create the template
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Templates → Create. Choose Manual to build the form yourself; review every field before using an imported or store template.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Add the field structure
requiredGuideSteps.body: Give the template a clear name, then add text, choice, number, date, GPS, photo, checkbox or icon fields. For a choice field, enter the permitted values.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set the collection order
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open each field to set its label, help text, required state and options. Use the up/down controls to put fields in field-work order, save, then run one test entry.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Edit safely
requiredGuideSteps.body: In Library → Templates, open the template menu and choose Edit. Save the changes, reopen the template and use Play or Use Template for new records.

entries.title: Run a live Team Session

requiredGuideSteps.title: Create the session
requiredGuideSteps.body: Settings → Team Tracking. On a phone or tablet, open Team and choose Create session. A Team account can host. An organization is optional; attach one only when the session belongs to that organization.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set the access details
requiredGuideSteps.body: Give the session a clear field name and set the name that will appear on the map. Choose a session password; MapNero generates the session code after creation. Send the generated code and password only to invited participants.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Join and finish safely
requiredGuideSteps.body: Each participant chooses Join session or scans the QR code, then enters the code, password and display name. Core, Pro and Team accounts can join. When field work ends, the host ends the session and does not reuse its code.

entries.title: Export field data and share it safely

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose what to export
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open the layer, track, map or report and choose Export. Select only the records you intend to send; use a recorded track for GPX and a GIS format for vector features.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose a compatible format
requiredGuideSteps.body: KML, GPX, CSV and KMZ are available on Free. GeoPDF and GeoTIFF need Core or higher. Shapefile, GeoPackage, DXF and QGIS/QField bundle need Pro or higher.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review and deliver
requiredGuideSteps.body: Check the selected layers, attributes, coordinates and attachments before generating the file. Use the system share sheet for a local file, or Share via Link only after checking that temporary public download is suitable.

entries.title: Configure MapNero settings

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose a working mode
requiredGuideSteps.body: Open Library → Settings → Usage Mode. Simple Map keeps the main workspace uncluttered; a specialist mode or Custom exposes the tools you choose. Your saved maps, layers and records remain intact.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Set language, appearance and units

requiredGuideSteps.title: Tune map and symbol preferences
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use Map Display for labels, grids, PDF boundary locking, collection behaviour and raster background choices. In Tools and Symbols, enable only the controls and symbol packs you want to see.

entries.title: Create a geofence

entries.title: GeoTIFF / PDF background

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open the georeferenced map

requiredGuideSteps.title: Choose the background

requiredGuideSteps.title: Find the map again

entries.title: Create a GeoPDF map layout

entries.title: Administer an organization

requiredGuideSteps.title: Open Administration

requiredGuideSteps.title: Invite with the minimum role

requiredGuideSteps.title: Complete first access on mobile
requiredGuideSteps.body: On iPhone, iPad or Android, open the invitation email, then open Organization under Account & Access in MapNero. Enter the invitation code from the email, the same email address, a password you choose and your display name; confirm the join. Use that email and password later at app.mapnero.com. If the app separately asks for email verification, follow its prompt; the sign-in code is not the organization invitation code.

requiredGuideSteps.title: Review and remove access
requiredGuideSteps.body: Use the pending list to cancel an unused invitation. Use Manage in the members list to change a role or remove a person. Do this before a device or account leaves the project.
